title: I've been building an AI powered Spine 2D alternative that makes rigging and animating characters incredibly easy
author: Crockiestar
selftext:
I've been working on **Warp Studio** for roughly two years and wanted to share a workflow I've been experimenting with in **Warp Puppet**.

The software has full **MCP support**, so you can connect frontier models like **Codex, Claude, or Gemini** to help rig and animate 2D characters. It's extremely easy to go from a character concept to a fully rigged animation with AI assistance, while still having full manual control over every part of the process.

One workflow I'm currently using involves having AI **draw characters with math** as separated movable parts on a sheet. Warp Puppet has really streamlined this, so you can go from **concept art to an editable rig to specific animations** very quickly. From there, I can use **Codex, Google Imagen, or other image models** to refine or redesign those parts while preserving their layout.

This lets me **quickly generate a near-infinite number of character variations that all share the same rig and animations**, including interchangeable body parts. You can **swap parts and keep your animations**, which makes it really fast to experiment with new character designs.

You can also **add effects like swipes**, or ask the AI to do it for you, then **see exactly how it did it inside the editor**. I think that's actually one of the coolest parts . You can learn a lot about animation by watching exactly what the AI is doing in a tool like this.

Warp Studio also supports a **game editor style testing environment**, **easy gravity**, and **hair physics**, which makes it much easier to preview motion. It works **surprisingly well for anime characters** too.

You can even **animate entire scenes**, and frontier models are honestly really good at **drawing scenes with math**, which makes it a fun space to experiment in. A workflow I’ve been enjoying lately is **drawing with math for concept art first, then using Codex or Google Imagen to refine on top**.

My goal with Warp Studio's Warp Puppet is to build a real **Spine 2D alternative**, but one built from the ground up with **MCP in mind**, so you and AI can actually **iteratively create and edit together**. It’s been kind of crazy seeing how quickly you can go from idea to animation without giving up creative control.

Check it out here:  [Warp Studio](https://crockiestar.itch.io/warp-studio)

replies.author: Crockiestar
replies.body:
Not sure what you mean? I still have all the Warp Studio save files for every example shown in the video, and I'd be happy to walk you through exactly how any of them were made.

As mentioned in the description, the most recent workflow I've been experimenting with is getting frontier models to mathematically draw characters while separating them into individual movable parts. Then I use ChatGPT's Imagen to refine those parts further. Warp Studio's Character Creator makes it pretty easy to bring that into the app, organize the pieces, and work with them. From there, I can simply have the AI rig and animate the character inside the software, which is what you are looking at in the video. If the results seem to good to be true I guess that's because they are pretty damn good at it. Its not always perfect but if you haven't used any of the frontier models like astra or Claude's Opus 5.5 this shouldn't be too surprising.

Everything shown is editable in Warp Studio, including the artwork parts, rigs, and animations, so it's not just a fake generated video or a one off result.
